name: pdk-dblift-schema
instr:
We're moving our services from Flyway to dblift. Copies of some of their SQLite databases are in /data/flyway/, and `dblift import-flyway` refuses several of them. Services that keep deploying with Flyway for a few more weeks get the import rerun after each Flyway deploy, and their dblift history ends up wrong, so `dblift migrate` reruns things Flyway already ran.

After an import, dblift_schema_history should hold every migration Flyway applied, failed, undid or marked deleted, plus the baseline if Flyway started from one, and nothing else. Rows keep the order Flyway applied them in and Flyway's values, with types named the way import-flyway already names them. Importing after every Flyway deploy, also after someone ran `flyway repair`, must leave the same rows as one import of Flyway's current history, so `dblift migrate` on the same scripts folder only runs what Flyway hasn't. Importing again with nothing new changes nothing, and rows dblift recorded itself are left alone. A history with a migration type dblift has no equivalent for is still refused, naming the type, with nothing imported.

Some databases were last migrated by old Flyway releases that kept the history under an older default table name. Plain `dblift import-flyway` should use that table when the current one doesn't exist.

The compatibility check, `client.executor.validator.validate_flyway_compatibility()` on a `DBLiftClient`, should agree with the import. It reports compatible right after an import and inc
